title: Exclude legacy/ from issue worktrees via sparse-checkout
goal: Apply sparse-checkout to every issue worktree so legacy/ is absent (except legacy/migrated/), eliminating the ~50% tree overhead from every repo-wide agent search, without affecting the operator's main checkout.

steps.description: Write the regression test first (TDD). tests/unit/worktree-sparse-legacy-test.sh builds a real git repo with a legacy/ tree (including legacy/migrated/sentinel.md), calls zbuild_worktree_acquire and zbuild_worktree_enter, then asserts: (a) legacy/ content is absent except legacy/migrated/; (b) legacy/migrated/ files are present; (c) a branch switch inside the worktree retains the exclusion; (d) a second zbuild_worktree_acquire call (reuse path) retains the exclusion; (e) git -C <repo_root> config core.sparseCheckout is not 'true' in the main checkout after the operation. This test must fail (red) at the merge-base before any implementation change.

Add sparse-checkout support to scripts/lib/worktree.sh. (a) New internal helper _zbuild_worktree_apply_sparse <wt> <repo_root>: enables extensions.worktreeConfig=true on the main repo's .git/config (per-worktree isolation; does not change main checkout's sparsity), then runs 'git -C "$wt" sparse-checkout set --no-cone /* !/legacy/ /legacy/migrated/' inside the linked worktree. (b) New public function zbuild_worktree_include_legacy_path <wt> <path>: calls 'git -C "$wt" sparse-checkout add "$path"' to widen the sparse set for a keeper PR that must read or git-rm a specific legacy source. (c) Call _zbuild_worktree_apply_sparse at the reuse return (zbuild_worktree_acquire line ~182) and after the new-tree post-condition check (line ~203). (d) Call _zbuild_worktree_apply_sparse at the reuse return (zbuild_worktree_enter line ~242) and after the new-tree creation (line ~282).

Amend ADR-059 §2 to record the sparse-checkout decision: add a paragraph under 'Why the worktree belongs to the issue' stating that legacy/ is excluded via per-worktree sparse-checkout (extensions.worktreeConfig) with legacy/migrated/ kept materialised, and that a run whose scope names a legacy/ path must call zbuild_worktree_include_legacy_path to widen the sparse set before operating on that path. Add the required '## Enforced by' section naming tests/unit/worktree-sparse-legacy-test.sh (new, §2 sparse exclusion), tests/unit/worktree-location-test.sh (§2 issue-keyed path shape, SPEC-9 through SPEC-11), and tests/unit/legacy-e1-tombstone-test.sh (§2 legacy/migrated/ intact). Then remove ADR-059-issue-vs-run-keying.md from config/adr-enforcement-baseline.txt so lint-adr-enforced-by.sh stops exempting it.

notes: Sparse-checkout pattern rationale: '/*' includes everything by default; '!/legacy/' excludes the entire legacy tree; '/legacy/migrated/' re-includes only the tombstone subdirectory. This is a no-cone pattern (--no-cone) because the default cone mode would not correctly handle negation patterns. extensions.worktreeConfig must be set on the main repo before the per-worktree sparse-checkout file is written; without it, git writes a shared sparse-checkout file and ALL worktrees (including the operator's main checkout) become sparse. Setting extensions.worktreeConfig is safe and additive — it does not alter any existing checkout; it only enables per-WT config files going forward. The guard test for 'main checkout not made sparse' checks git -C repo_root config core.sparseCheckout and asserts it is absent or false. The keeper-PR widening function (zbuild_worktree_include_legacy_path) is explicitly requested by the issue ('say how') but is not yet called by any engine code — the call site is in the engine's scope-reading stage, which is out of scope for this issue. The function ships but the caller is a follow-up. Branch-switch retention: once sparse-checkout is set via worktreeConfig, it persists through git checkout calls inside the linked worktree — this is a property of git's sparse-checkout mechanism, not something zbuild needs to actively maintain. The test verifies it. ADR-002 is not amended here because the sparse-checkout decision is a worktree-materialisation property (§2 of ADR-059), not a change to the sentinel protocol or the pruning protocol that ADR-002 governs. The issue references 'ADR-002' only as context for the established legacy/ exclusion convention, not as the locus of the new statement.
